Express tiers as profiles keyed by family/action and by descriptor cap; choose by [caps] and initialize.clientInfo.name, never by a runtime call (listChanged stays false); per-profile byte report. This IS P-agent-parity.tool-profile and CP-mcp-profiles: fold them in, do not duplicate (close them as done-by when this lands). Source: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-tool-diet.md section 9. Conformance: declared-command matrix stays the single source (CLI/MCP parity), files under 20 KB, no private addresses or keys in tracked files.

DECIDED 2026-10-22 (operator, D-mcp-tool-families; docs/ddflow/decisions/mcp-tool-diet.md): profiles lean (15 tools), families (24, the default), hot+families (36); flat tiers opt-in; chosen from descriptor cap and clientInfo.name, never a runtime call.

WIRING OWED (impl-tool-diet, from MTD-aliases review): on a connection whose profile advertises the families (families, hot+families, lean), a call by an old tool name must append tools.aliases.alias_for(name) to the call's used aliases so the existing Notices loop says it once per session ("note: tool 'ddflow_gate_record' is deprecated since 0.2.8; use 'ddflow_gate action=record'"). Not on flat/legacy profiles. Test through Server.handle that the note text is in the first result and absent from the second.

Folded CP-mcp-profiles (Lean MCP profiles worker, reviewer and operator with documented allow-lists, selectable per host): MTD-profiles body says 'This IS CP-mcp-profiles: fold them in, do not duplicate'; yet it needed them (unrealisable: they close only when it lands). D-mcp-tool-families (operator 2026-10-22) defines the profiles..

The tool list byte budget is nearly full and hosts apply tool policies; profiles are data (a config table), generated docs list each; selected by env, file or the connect URL; reuses the MCP tool-list machinery of B-lean-and-trusted. Every control-plane kit uses the worker profile.

Extends P-agent-parity.tool-profile (tool-count profiles per agent): ONE profile table keyed by role (worker, reviewer, operator) and by agent, not two.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds (kind, template, gate, lens, role, lint set, importer, pack, job) is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

[vocabulary] maps kind names to the project's terms (singular, plural); CLI output, MCP reply text, prompts, the brief and exported documents use them; event kinds, JSON keys and canonical MCP tool names stay as they are so tooling and replay do not break; CLI accepts the project's term as an alias for the kind in commands (ddflow story add = task add). Per D-id-schemes (operator 2026-10-05, 'Also CLI/MCP names'): MCP tools also accept project-worded alias names (calls by alias always accepted; aliases advertised in tools/list only when the tool tier allows, the list has a budget); the parity test treats an alias as its canonical command.

data.decision: Retired by supersession, history kept, because each one's own text or the queue state proves it spent: D1 is a test artefact (title 'D', body 'use it', glob a.py); D-usage-pacing-2026-10 says 'until the Oct 15 usage reset' and today is 2026-10-23, yet its glob docs/ddflow/decisions/** tells every decision-document task 'light work only'; D-unify-first says every not-yet-started task waits for P-unify, which is done (217/217), and its glob .ddflow/events/** matched every event-log edit. No rule changes: nothing here binds new work. Other spent-looking decisions (D-cleanup-before-pause, D-cleanup-accept-bar, D-dry-run-from-running-version, D-bug-override-accepted-2026-10-11, D-audit-calls-2026-10-10, D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted) have narrow globs and stay for the operator to retire (see docs/ddflow/research/queue-dedupe-2026-10-23.md).
